gen_risks.description: Insufficient MRV and validation capacity may lead to inaccurate GHG reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure dedicated funding for validation throughout the project, build early MRV capacity, and contract reputable independent validators.
gen_risks.evidence: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification of results will be conducted by qualified, independent validation entities

gen_risks.description: PFIs may lack technical capacity to assess green loans adequately.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance, develop standard green‑loan appraisal tools, and monitor PFIs’ compliance with action plans.
gen_risks.evidence: The credit line will be channeled exclusively through PFIs … with an action plan required where capacity is medium.

gen_risks.description: Financial‑management inefficiencies due to legacy information systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade FM systems, automate reconciliations, and conduct periodic external audits to ensure timely and accurate reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: Residual FM risk is assessed as Moderate… efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

gen_risks.description: High credit risk of beneficiary enterprises and PFIs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply rigorous credit assessments, use risk‑sharing instruments (guarantees, collateral), and set prudent loan‑to‑value limits.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second‑tier operations

gen_risks.description: Delay in adopting the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear adoption milestones, provide technical support, and link disbursements to documented adoption of the manual.
gen_risks.evidence: The Borrower shall adopt the Project Operations Manual… condition of loan effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Low uptake of financing, especially by women‑led firms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct outreach, simplify application procedures, introduce gender‑focused incentives, and monitor uptake regularly.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk of financing being available but uptake limited, especially for women‑owned firms.

gen_risks.description: NAFIN’s limited direct procurement experience may cause non‑compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified internal procurement officer, deliver hands‑on training, and ensure close Bank supervision of procurement processes.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes

gen_risks.description: Policy or regulatory changes affecting the Sustainable Taxonomy or Plan México.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous dialogue with government, embed flexibility clauses, and align project activities with the Sustainable Taxonomy.
gen_risks.evidence: The operation aims to support the goals of Plan México … and uses Mexico’s Sustainable Taxonomy

gen_risks.description: Green‑washing risk if sustainability plans are not properly validated.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate third‑party validation, conduct random audits, and publicly disclose verification outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification

gen_risks.description: Physical climate risks (heat, drought) may increase loan delinquency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilience criteria in loan design, promote insurance products, and perform climate stress‑testing.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms

gen_risks.description: Private capital mobilisation may fall short of the US$89 M target.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer co‑financing incentives, develop market‑development activities, and consider partial guarantees to attract private investors.
gen_risks.evidence: The Project will help mobilize private capital … expected to leverage at least US$89 million

gen_risks.description: Fraud or corruption despite anti‑corruption provisions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen anti‑corruption monitoring, implement whistle‑blower mechanisms, and conduct regular compliance audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Loan Agreement includes provisions for preventing, detecting, reporting, investigation, remediation and otherwise addressing fraud and corruption

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
